title: Minimize Array Sum Using Divisible Replacements
summary: Given an integer array, you can repeatedly choose two indices where one element is divisible by the other, then replace the divisible element with the divisor.
statement: Given an integer array, you can repeatedly choose two indices where one element is divisible by the other, then replace the divisible element with the divisor. The goal is to find the minimum possible sum of the array after performing any number of such operations.
constraints: nums is nonempty and contains positive values up to 100,000.
A value may be replaced by another currently present value that divides it.
Return the minimum sum after any number of replacements.
hints: Operations never introduce a value outside the initial value set.
Each original value can independently reach the smallest initially present divisor of that value.
Sieve every present divisor across its multiples, recording the minimum.
Keeping a divisor occurrence unchanged makes it permanently available, so all independent minima are simultaneously attainable.
editorial: Keeping a divisor occurrence unchanged makes it permanently available, so all independent minima are simultaneously attainable.

tests.explanation: Six can become two; neither three nor two can decrease, producing sum seven.
Four and eight become two while three remains, producing [2,2,2,3] with sum nine.
